turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on a, an and the?
turns.tutor:
Look at this example: I have a pen. She eats an apple.
"Pen" starts with a "p" sound, so we say "a". "Apple" starts with an "a" sound, so we say "an".
The rule: use "an" before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u) and "a" before other sounds.
Right: I see an egg. Wrong: I see a egg.

Now you try. Write one word:
Write a or an: She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
turns.judgeInput:

C1 (correct) strength 0: a singular countable noun needs a/an (or the). Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: an before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
